title: Why averaging many trees improves regression

items.stem: A random forest averages many deep regression trees. What is the main reason the average predicts new data better than a single deep tree?

options.text: It removes bias, so each tree ends up closer to the truth
It cuts variance, since errors of different trees partly cancel
It enlarges the training set, so every tree sees more rows
It deepens the model, so splits capture finer data patterns

items.stem: Each tree in a forest has prediction variance 144 at a given point, and any two trees have correlation 0.25. The forest averages B = 12 trees. What is the variance of the forest's prediction at that point?
A forest of 100 trees has a variance floor that is too high, because its trees are strongly correlated. Which change lowers that floor the most?

options.text: Raising the number of trees from 100 to 10,000
Growing every tree deeper so it fits more closely
Letting each split consider fewer random features
Training every tree on exactly the same sample

items.stem: Single trees have prediction variance 50 and pairwise correlation 0.4. As the number of trees grows without limit, what value does the variance of the forest's average approach?
Two trees make exactly the same errors on every point, so their correlation is 1. In one or two sentences, say what averaging them does to the variance, and why.
